title: The Warning to Make GNP Seguros Stadium Debut in 2027: ‘We’ve Dreamed & Worked So Hard to Reach This Moment’
summary: The Villarreal Vélez sisters will become the first all-female band to perform at the iconic stadium in the Mexico City.
contentText:
The Warning will perform for the first time at Estadio GNP Seguros in Mexico City on Feb. 5, 2027, becoming the first all-female Mexican band to take the stage at the iconic stadium. The concert will be part of their Everything’s Falling World Tour.

“OUR FIRST STADIUM!!! We’ve dreamed and worked so hard to reach this moment, we still can’t believe it’s finally happening,” wrote the rock band made up of sisters Daniela, Paulina and Alejandra Villarreal in a social media post , in Spanish. “See you at Estadio GNP Seguros on February 5, 2027!”

Related

According to promoter OCESA, ticket presales for the concert will be available through Ticketmaster Mexico on Sept. 9 and 10 for HSBC bank customers, with general sales beginning on Sept. 11.

The announcement of their performance at the emblematic venue (previously known as Foro Sol) comes just one day after The Warning was revealed as the headlining act for the halftime show of this year’s NFL game in Mexico City between the Minnesota Vikings and the San Francisco 49ers. The news also follows the release of their fifth album , Everything’s Falling , last Friday (Aug. 28).

Among the band’s recent achievements, they became the first Mexican group and the first all-female band to top Billboard ’s Mainstream Rock Airplay chart with their song “Kerosene,” which leads the ranking dated Sept. 5.

The Warning’s repertoire is predominantly in English, their second language. The group hails from Monterrey, a city in northern Mexico near the U.S. border.

This year, the powerful trio continues their global rise with performances in the U.S. after touring Europe, Asia and South America. They’ve also made appearances at major festivals worldwide and held their own headlining shows.

Among their latest releases is a duet with regional Mexican superstar Carín León titled “Love To Be Loved” that blends country music and hard rock.
